A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same religious-trajectory analysis of Holocaust testimonies. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. Appendices A–L are retained, and v5 adds Appendix M.

before.justification: v4 reports original classifier evaluations, trajectory analysis of 1,000 testimonies, human evaluation of clustering, and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports classification confusion matrices in Appendix M, Figure 13.

M1.justification: Sections 4–6 retain the same segmentation, RoBERTa filtering, GPT/Mistral classification, trajectory taxonomy and DTW-based clustering procedures. The annotation guidelines and prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same 1,000 English Shoah Foundation testimonies and religious practice/belief tasks, including the retained supplementary subsets. The new confusion matrices concern the existing classification tasks; no additional dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 6 retains the same GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, mini/nano and Mistral variants and prompting conditions. Tables 3 and 8–10 retain their respective artificial-trajectory comparator sets and topic/thesaurus references.

E3.justification: The stated preprocessing, data splits, training budgets, model settings, F1 and trajectory-distance evaluations, and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged. Figure 13 adds diagnostic breakdowns without documenting a revised testing protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix M and Figure 13 analyze confusion between classification labels. Section 8 also adds a Christian-prayer misclassification example. Existing filtering comparisons, trajectory-density analyses and clustering examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-split cross-validation, seed information, agreement estimates, DTW standard deviations and t-tests. The added confusion matrices introduce no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing table values and trajectory distributions are unchanged. Figure 13 newly reports class-confusion proportions, including 0.64 for belief Other predicted as Positive and 0.56 for practice Other predicted as Active. Section 8 additionally reports positive-valence predictions for Christian prayers.

T1.justification: The trajectory formalization in Section 3, min_sum_dist definition in Section 5.2, and taxonomy and coverage definitions in Table 2 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: extracting and clustering religious trajectories, identifying common belief/practice structures, and demonstrating NLP for character development. Added historical motivation and diagnostic evidence do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v4's existing stereotype-bias warning, v5 Section 8 links observed classification errors to possible positivity bias and discusses pretraining stereotypes and Christian-prayer errors. The Limitations section newly names survivorship bias alongside retained reporting-bias caveats.

D1.justification: Model versions, training hyperparameters, prompts, clustering-library settings and annotation instructions are retained. The Ethical Considerations section preserves the same code-on-request and archive-controlled data/model access conditions.

R1.justification: v5 expands contextual positioning with literature on faith stability/change after trauma, computational historical research, model bias and survivorship. Examples include Berkovits, Leo et al., Ashwin et al. and Chen et al. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds targeted introductory and discussion paragraphs and a short Appendix M, with localized wording, acknowledgment and bibliographic corrections. The overall section order and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 13 adds two confusion-matrix heatmaps. Table 1 has revised column widths and wrapping, and existing material shifts with pagination; Figure 12 now shares the final page with Figure 13. Figures 1–12 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4's general bias warnings, v5 provides concrete classification-error evidence in Figure 13 and connects it to caution when interpreting trajectory patterns. Historical context and the survivorship caveat also improve interpretation. The gain is limited: Figure 13 leaves the evaluated model unspecified, and the effect of these errors on the retained trajectory conclusions is not quantified.
